title: Structure-preserving reduced-order models of thin panels in supersonic and hypersonic flow
abstract: arXiv:2610.31504v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We build structure-preserving reduced-order models for both challenge problems of the AePW-4 High-Speed Working Group. They are a clamped thin panel at Mach 1.92 (RC-19) and a cantilever plate at Mach 5.85 (HyMAX). The published data for each case hold no time-resolved response and no repeated runs. The physics must therefore be carried by the form of the model. One construction gives two models per problem. A Ritz-Galerkin reference model describes the plate. A learned model keeps the reference model's exact potential, fits the remaining generalized forces, and trains only a dissipation that cannot add energy. Its energy balance holds for any weights by construction. On the trained model the worst relative residual is 2.2e-15. On RC-19, shock relations predict a pressure ratio of 1.521 across the panel. Pressure-sensitive paint measured the same value. Thirty runs of the learned model place the mean dominant frequency within 1.0% of t

translated_title: 超声速与高超声速气流中薄板的结构保持降阶模型
translated_abstract: 我们为AePW-4高速工作组的两个挑战问题构建了结构保持的降阶模型。这两个问题分别是马赫1.92下的固支薄板（RC-19）和马赫5.85下的悬臂板（HyMAX）。每个算例的公开数据既没有时间分辨的响应，也没有重复运行的结果，因此物理特性必须由模型的形式本身来承载。通过一种构造方法，每个问题得到两个模型：一个描述板的Ritz-Galerkin参考模型，以及一个学习模型——后者保留参考模型的精确势能，拟合剩余的广义力，并且只训练一个无法注入能量的耗散项。其能量平衡在构造上对任意权重均成立。在训练后的模型上，最差相对残差为2.2e-15。在RC-19算例中，激波关系预测板两侧的压力比为1.521，压敏漆测量得到了相同的数值。学习模型的三十次运行使平均主导频率与（原文在此处截断）的偏差控制在1.0%以内。
tldr: 本文为AePW-4高速工作组的两个挑战问题（马赫1.92固支薄板与马赫5.85悬臂板）构建了结构保持的降阶模型，其学习模型在构造上严格保证能量平衡（最差相对残差仅2.2e-15），并准确复现了激波压力比1.521（与压敏漆实测一致）和主频（偏差小于1.0%）。
en_tdlr: This paper builds structure-preserving reduced-order models for the two AePW-4 challenge problems (a clamped thin panel at Mach 1.92 and a cantilever plate at Mach 5.85), where the learned model preserves energy balance by construction (worst relative residual 2.2e-15) and accurately reproduces the shock pressure ratio of 1.521 (matching pressure-sensitive paint measurements) and dominant frequencies within 1.0%.
